title: Lameta Formation, India: titanosaur nests
summary: The Maastrichtian Lameta Formation of the Narmada Valley, central India, is known for dinosaur eggs. In Dhar District researchers documented 92 titanosaur clutches holding 256 eggs of six oospecies, in rocks formed in a semi-arid river and lake setting that lie below, and in places between, the earliest Deccan Traps lava flows.

uncertainty.note: Sources give only "Maastrichtian"; the pin dates are a placement within that stage, not a measured age.

importance.justification: One of the largest known dinosaur nesting regions, with titanosaur clutches across the Narmada Valley.
